title: The controlled-profile scaffold is deterministic and the app it generates builds
description:
SPIDR child 1 of task-5ef1a0a9010c4bfe872ff9b774068234 (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05). Dependency-free LEAF and the highest-risk piece: everything else in the parent is a command wrapper around this generator.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: a DETERMINISTIC scaffold generator for the controlled profile, pinned by a profile version constant, and the proof that what it emits actually builds. No command kind, no git, no UI - children 2 and 3.

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-20a6d1eb: no product scaffold exists. `grep -rn 'repository\\.bootstrap|CONTROLLED_PROFILE|scaffold' --include=*.ts apps/ packages/` finds only `moe init`, which scaffolds a STORE, an operator credential and moe.config.json (cli/moe-cli-main.ts:16,58) - not a product. `project.bind_repository` binds an EXISTING repository. The gap is real.

THE PROFILE (VISION 'one controlled product profile first'): TypeScript; React + Vite web; Node API; PostgreSQL via docker-compose; vitest; Playwright; pnpm workspace; GitHub Actions CI running `pnpm typecheck && pnpm test`; `.env.example`; README carrying the product name.

DETERMINISM IS THE CONTRACT. Every product must start IDENTICAL for a given profile version, or the loop's later claims (the verifier recipe, the deployment requirements, the migration tool) stop holding across products. Pin the generated tree with a GOLDEN TEST under a profile version constant, and make the only variable input explicit (the product name) so a diff of two scaffolds differs in exactly the places it should.

THE HARD PART IS DoD 2's SECOND HALF: the generated app must actually pass `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm build` IN A TEST THAT RUNS IT. That is a slow, network-touching, disk-heavy test - design it deliberately: a single run in a temp directory, with the child run's own count lines captured and quoted. A golden tree that has never been built is a file list, not a working scaffold, and this clause is what stops shipping one.
definitionOfDone: A golden test pins the EXACT generated file tree plus the bytes of package.json, the docker-compose file and the CI workflow, under a named profile version constant. Two generations with the same inputs are byte-identical; two generations differing only in product name differ ONLY where the name appears - assert that as a diff, not by eyeballing.

THE GENERATED APP BUILDS: a test generates into a temp directory and runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm build`, quoting the CHILD run's own count lines. A golden tree that was never built is a file list; this is the clause that makes it a scaffold. Record the wall-clock cost in the step note so a later row can decide whether to gate it differently.

`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` implies a COMMITTED LOCKFILE in the scaffold: assert one is generated and that the install does not need to resolve it. A scaffold whose first install rewrites its own lockfile is not deterministic.

The profile version constant is the single source: an unknown version refuses BOOTSTRAP_PROFILE_VERSION_UNKNOWN with its layer (the code is defined here even though child 2 raises it at the command edge - say so in the record rather than manufacturing a call site).
The CI workflow the scaffold emits runs `pnpm typecheck && pnpm test` - assert the workflow bytes contain both, since a scaffold that ships a CI file that does not actually gate is worse than none.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Quote the generated app's own gate output separately and label it as the CHILD run, so the two are never confused.
taskRails: DETERMINISM IS THE CONTRACT. Same profile version plus same product name must yield byte-identical trees. No timestamps, no random ids, no host paths, no tool versions read from the host baked into generated files.
THE GENERATED APP MUST BE BUILT, not just written. A file-tree golden test alone cannot tell a working scaffold from a broken one.
NO COMMAND KIND, NO GIT, NO UI: `repository.bootstrap`, `git init`, the first commit, the optional `gh repo create` and the binding are child 2; the browser form is child 3.
PIN THE PROFILE VERSION and treat the scaffold as an artifact of it. A change to the tree is a version bump, not an edit in place, because later rows depend on knowing what a product started as.
FEATURES ONLY (inherited): no security-boundary or policy work.

Step 6 asserts that two-path set as a computed diff.

implementationPlan.description:
ASSEMBLY HALF of controlled-profile-generator.ts. Add `generateControlledProfile({ productName, profileVersion })` returning the result type from step 1.

ORDER OF CHECKS: profileVersion is validated FIRST, before the product name, so `BOOTSTRAP_PROFILE_VERSION_UNKNOWN` is reachable even when both inputs are bad. Step 6 asserts that precedence.

The returned map is built in SORTED PATH ORDER (UTF-16 code-unit compare on the forward-slash path, not `localeCompare` — locale-dependent ordering would make the golden manifest host-dependent). Paths are forward-slash relative, never absolute, never host-separated.

The generator returns DATA ONLY — a `ReadonlyMap<string, string>`. It never touches the filesystem to write. Its only read is the lockfile asset.

LOCKFILE: read `assets/controlled-profile-v1-lock.yaml` with `readFileSync(new URL("./assets/controlled-profile-v1-lock.yaml", import.meta.url), "utf8")` and normalize `\r\n` -> `\n` BEFORE emitting it as the tree's `pnpm-lock.yaml`. A CRLF checkout of the asset must not change the emitted bytes. Create `assets/controlled-profile-v1-lock.yaml` as an empty placeholder in this step; step 5 mints the real one.

Product-name substitution is a single explicit call site per name-bearing file (root package.json, README.md) — do not run a blanket string replace over the whole tree, or a future template that happens to contain the name string would silently join the diff set.
implementationPlan.note:
ASSEMBLY HALF landed. `generateControlledProfile(request): ControlledProfileResult` added to controlled-profile-generator.ts (138 physical lines total, target <=250).

ORDER OF CHECKS pinned in code and PROVEN by probe, not by reading: version first, then name. Probe `generateControlledProfile({ productName: "Bad Name", profileVersion: "controlled-999" })` -> `{"ok":false,"code":"BOOTSTRAP_PROFILE_VERSION_UNKNOWN","refusedBy":"DAEMON_INGRESS"}`. Both inputs were invalid and the VERSION code won, which is the precedence step 6 asserts.

SORT: `entries.sort(([left],[right]) => left < right ? -1 : left > right ? 1 : 0)` — raw UTF-16 code-unit compare on the forward-slash path. Deliberately NOT localeCompare: a locale-dependent order would make the golden manifest differ between hosts, which is the exact failure this row exists to prevent. Paths are forward-slash relative; no absolute, no host separator.

DATA ONLY: no fs WRITE anywhere in the module; the single fs read is the lockfile asset. No module-level mutable state, so two concurrent calls cannot interfere (every template is a frozen module const or a pure function of the name).

LOCKFILE: `const LOCKFILE_ASSET = new URL("./assets/controlled-profile-v1-lock.yaml", import.meta.url)` read with `readFileSync(LOCKFILE_ASSET, "utf8").replaceAll("\r\n", "\n")`. Normalizing on READ is what keeps a CRLF checkout of the asset from changing the emitted bytes. `assets/controlled-profile-v1-lock.yaml` created as an EMPTY placeholder in this step; step 5 mints the real bytes.

NAME SUBSTITUTION is two explicit call sites — `controlledProfileRootFiles(productName)` interpolates into root package.json and README.md and nothing else; `controlledProfilePackageFiles()` takes no argument at all. No blanket string replace over the assembled tree, so a future template containing the same string cannot silently join the name-diff set.

implementationPlan.description:
MINT THE REAL LOCKFILE ASSET. This is a one-shot act, not a test.

1. Generate the tree to a temp directory with the lockfile entry omitted.
2. Run `pnpm install --lockfile-only` in that directory with this repo's pnpm 11.0.8.
3. Copy the produced `pnpm-lock.yaml` byte-for-byte into `apps/daemon/src/repository/controlled-profile/assets/controlled-profile-v1-lock.yaml`, normalized to LF.
4. `rmSync(tempDir, { recursive: true, force: true })` on EVERY exit path including the failing one (epic rail 4).

THEN PROVE THE ASSET IS PRODUCT-AGNOSTIC — this is the property the whole static-asset design rests on:
- `grep -n "^importers:" -A 6` the asset and confirm the importer keys are the three DIRECTORY paths `.`, `packages/api`, `packages/web`. pnpm keys importers by directory, not by package name.
- `grep -c "<the product name you used>" assets/controlled-profile-v1-lock.yaml` must be 0. If it is not, the lockfile cannot be a static asset and you must stop and report rather than special-casing it.

Record in the step note: the exact pnpm version used, the `lockfileVersion:` line from the asset, and the byte size. A later profile-version bump re-runs exactly this step.

PRODUCT-AGNOSTIC PROPERTY MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED — this is what the whole static-asset design rests on:
- `awk '/^importers:/{f=1;next} /^[a-z]/{f=0} f && /^  [^ ]/{print}'` over the asset -> exactly three keys: `.:`, `packages/api:`, `packages/web:`. All three are DIRECTORY paths. pnpm keys importers by directory, never by package name, so one asset serves every product.

The asset's `settings:` block records `autoInstallPeers: false` — it matches the emitted pnpm-workspace.yaml, which is a precondition for `--frozen-lockfile` not re-resolving (a settings mismatch is one of the ways pnpm decides a lockfile is stale).

FORWARD NOTE FOR CHILD 2 (the `repository.bootstrap` command row) AND FOR THE EPIC-FINAL ROW task-99f364e3a6104ee993b6820c580a52fb — PACKAGING OF THE LOCKFILE ASSET.

The plan flagged a suspected packaging gap: a `.yaml` asset under apps/daemon/src may not be enumerated by tools/packaging/pack-source.ts, shipping an installed artifact whose generator cannot read its own lockfile. I MEASURED it instead of forwarding the guess. Three of the four failure modes are REFUTED; one real risk remains and it is not the one named.

REFUTED 1 - pack-source is extension-agnostic. `PACK_SOURCE_ARCHIVE_PATHSPEC` (tools/packaging/pack-source-integrity.ts:28) is `[".", ":(exclude)<PACK_SOURCE_RUNTIME_STATE_ROOT>"]`, fed to `git archive`. There is no extension allowlist anywhere in that path. The asset ships iff it is git-TRACKED — which it is, since it is reported in complete_step.modifiedFiles and lands in this row's commit.

REFUTED 2 - the asset is not classified as a secret. Probed against the PRODUCTION predicate, not by reading the regex:
  isSensitivePackSourcePath("apps/daemon/src/repository/controlled-profile/assets/controlled-profile-v1-lock.yaml") -> false
  isSensitivePackSourcePath("pnpm-lock.yaml") -> false
This mattered: `yaml`/`yml` ARE in SECRET_DOCUMENT_EXTENSIONS (pack-source-sensitive.ts:5), so the extension alone put the asset one predicate away from a PACK_SENSITIVE_PATH_PRESENT refusal. It survives because the stem `controlled-profile-v1-lock` matches neither EXACT_SECRET_STEMS nor SENSITIVE_DOCUMENT_STEM. NAMING CONSTRAINT FOR A FUTURE PROFILE BUMP: do not rename the asset to anything whose stem contains `auth`, `credential(s)`, `secret(s)`, `token(s)`, `api-key`, `access-key` or `service-account` as a `[-_.]`-delimited part — that would make packaging refuse the release.

REFUTED 3 - the asset is not mistaken for a test artifact. Probed against the production classifier:
  isTestArtifact(".../assets/controlled-profile-v1-lock.yaml") -> false
  isTestArtifact(".../controlled-profile-generator.ts") -> false
  isTestArtifact(".../controlled-profile-generator.js") -> false
  isTestArtifact(".../controlled-profile-generator.test.ts") -> true   (same as the existing sibling apps/daemon/src/repository/publish-ledger.test.ts -> true)
So production modules and the asset ship, the two .test.ts files are stripped, and this row introduces no new classification class.

THE REAL RESIDUAL RISK, for child 2 to carry: tools/packaging/distribution-inventory.ts is a HAND-MAINTAINED roster of explicit asset paths, not a directory walk (see PROVIDER_CLAUDE_ASSETS and its comment about a directory walk finding fixtures). `grep -c "apps/daemon/src/repository/" tools/packaging/distribution-inventory.ts` -> 0, so today the whole repository/ directory is outside that roster and this row is not a new exception. But when child 2 wires `repository.bootstrap` into the SHIPPED daemon closure, whatever backfills that roster must add SEVEN paths, not three:

  controlled-profile-root-templates.ts + .js
  controlled-profile-package-templates.ts + .js
  assets/controlled-profile-v1-lock.yaml    <- the one a ".ts files under the new directory" sweep silently drops
A roster missing only the asset produces the exact failure the plan feared: an installed artifact that loads, resolves and typechecks, and then throws ENOENT from `readFileSync(new URL("./assets/...", import.meta.url))` the first time a human bootstraps a product. 1. OPT-IN GATE VACUITY. The expensive arm is `it.runIf(process.env.MOE_SCAFFOLD_BUILD === "1")`. A skipped test that is called a pass is a false completion claim. Three things stop that here: (i) an ALWAYS-ON companion arm in the same file asserts the preconditions the expensive arm depends on, so the file is never a no-op; (ii) DoD 6 forces the worker to run it WITH the flag and quote the child's own count lines, which a skip cannot produce; (iii) step 8 requires quoting `Test Files 1 passed` AND a zero skipped count from that run. Reason for the opt-in at all: an unconditional multi-minute network install inside `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` -- the standard gate every row on this board runs -- would red on any offline host and make every later gate inadmissible (epic rail 4). DoD 2's "so a later row can decide whether to gate it differently" is exactly this decision left open.
2. VACUOUS CHILD GATE. `pnpm test` in the generated app prints "No test files found" and EXITS 0 when no tests exist. The child run's evidence is the `Test Files N passed` line with N >= 1, never the exit code. Step 3 requires each generated package to ship a real assertion for this reason.
3. FROZEN LOCKFILE DRIFT. `--frozen-lockfile` fails if the resolving pnpm differs in major from the one that minted the asset, or if any generated package.json carries a RANGE rather than an exact version. Step 2 pins `packageManager` and uses exact versions only. Any later edit to a generated package.json is a lockfile re-mint plus a golden re-bake -- and per task rail 4 a profile version BUMP, not an edit in place.
4. HOST NONDETERMINISM. `Date`, `crypto`, `process.cwd()`, `os.EOL`, path separators and any host tool version read at runtime are forbidden inside the generator. The step-9 mutation drill is what actually proves the golden is load-bearing.

6. TEMP LEAK. `rmSync(dir,{recursive:true,force:true})` must run in a `finally`, not after the assertions -- a throwing leg would otherwise leave a full node_modules tree behind (epic rail 4).

PACKAGING BLIND SPOT (flag forward, NOT this row's fix): `tools/packaging/pack-source.ts` enumerates daemon source; a `.yaml` asset under apps/daemon/src may not be picked up, which would ship an installed artifact whose generator cannot read its own lockfile. Raise it as a comment for child 2 / the epic-final row task-99f364e3a6104ee993b6820c580a52fb rather than widening this plan.
8. DRILL RESTORE. Every file in this plan is NEW (untracked), so `git diff -- <file>` is EMPTY before, during and after a mutation and certifies nothing. Step 9 requires `git status --porcelain` on the exact mutated paths first, and a SHA256 equality proof against an out-of-tree backup in a call separate from the restore.
